It reflects the deeply rooted belief in preserving and nurturing life, emphasizing the concept that every life is precious and worthy of respect.

historical_references.reference: Pranika was a legendary figure in Hindu mythology, known as the goddess of the northern direction and the protector of cows.
historical_references.context: Pranika is mentioned in various Hindu scriptures and Puranas, particularly in the context of the directions and the protection of cows, which were considered sacred in ancient Indian culture.

historical_references.reference: Another reference to Pranika can be found in the Mahabharata, where she is mentioned as the mother of the horse Kesava, who was a crucial part of the epic battle of Kurukshetra.
